sleep_gaps.note: A night the watch missed can be filled in with `python3 log_sleep.py <date> <hours>`. Sleep duration is recoverable that way; the overnight heart-rate series is not, so the nocturnal drop stays unavailable for those nights.

unavailable_signals.reason: Both get_hrv_data and get_hrv_data_range return empty for this account — this watch does not record it. The nocturnal heart-rate drop, derived from the overnight series, stands in for it.

available_signals.reason: In use on 14 of the last 14 nights — roughly one sample every two minutes. This is where the nocturnal-drop signal comes from, standing in for HRV.

readiness.label: Recovery signals are strong — take the session as planned.

load.label: Load is in the productive range against your 4-week baseline.
load.method: Banister TRIMP from average HR where available, per-sport rate otherwise.

form.label: Productive training: carrying fatigue but absorbing it.
form.method: EWMA, 42-day fitness / 7-day fatigue, seeded from the first 6 weeks of available load. Form is judged as a share of fitness so the bands don't depend on the load unit.

garmin.note: VO2 max and race predictions are Garmin's own models, stored each sync so they build a trend the API won't give you.

projection.note: Riegel extrapolation (exponent 1.06) from training runs of 5+ miles in the last 6 weeks. Riegel assumes a maximal effort, so a projection off training runs reads pessimistic — treat it as a floor, not a forecast.

ironman.note: Extrapolated from one completed 70.3 by slowing each leg's pace and applying it over the full distance, plus 15 minutes of transitions. Conventional fade factors, not measurements — a first full distance has real spread, which is why this is a range.
ironman.name: Ironman (140.6)

insights: The run is where the time is. Your 70.3 half went 8:33/mi off the bike; at full distance the same fitness projects 4:11:04 to 4:46:56 for the marathon. Every minute per mile you take off standalone marathon pace is roughly 26 minutes here.
You rode the 70.3 at 18.9 mph. Held at full-distance intensity that is 6:17:22 to 6:45:50 for 112 miles — the single largest block of the day, and the one that decides what is left for the run.

Last 8 weeks: 136 minutes swimming and 252 minutes riding. The marathon block is deliberately run-only, so both are near zero by design — worth knowing rather than worrying about, but the clock on rebuilding them starts the day after the marathon.

nutrition.note: Protein held flat at 1g per lb. Intake is not tracked — Garmin carries no food log — so these are targets, not a record of what you ate.
